sections.content:
Level 1 rule: click (r,c) → block's top-left corner = (r-1, c-1). That is, the click position = the block's bottom-right corner. The block teleports so that its bottom-right lands on the click position. All of Level 1's clicks were on the diagonal from the block: click (53,10) → block (52-54, 9-11); click (51,12) → (50-52,11-13); etc. Each click's bottom-right = click position. And the clicks were all on the same NE diagonal: (53,10), (51,12), (49,14)... Δ=(-2,+2).
So the teleport is: the block's bottom-right → click position. But in Level 2, clicking (27,28) should place the square at (26-27, 27-28) — yet it didn't move. Why?
Difference: in Level 1, each click was on the NE diagonal extending from the block's current bottom-right. Block's bottom-right (60,5) → click (53,10): Δ=(-7,+5). Hmm, not on the diagonal. But the block moved to (52-54,9-11) — bottom-right (54,10), not (53,10)! Wait: click (53,10) → block bbox [52,9]..[54,9]?? The output says "block bbox [52, 9]..[54, 9]" — that's boundary[0]=[52,9] and boundary[-1]=[54,9]?? So the boundary's last point is [54,9], not [54,11]. The boundary is a list of corner points; boundary[-1] is not necessarily the bottom-right. For a 3x3 block at rows 52-54, cols 9-11, the clockwise boundary corners: [52,9],[52,11],[54,11],[54,9]. So boundary[-1]=[54,9] = bottom-left. OK, so the block is at (52-54, 9-11), bottom-right (54,11). Click was (53,10) = block center!
Let me redo: click (53,10) → block (52-54,9-11), center (53,10) = click. Click (51,12) → block (50-52,11-13), center (51,12) = click. So in Level 1, the block's center → click position. The block is 3x3 (odd), center = click.
Level 2: the square is 2x2 (even), no center cell. Click (37,18) → square (36-37,17-18): click = bottom-right. Click (27,28) → expected square (26-27,27-28) but didn't move.
Hmm! So for the 2x2 square, the click = bottom-right corner. Click (27,28) should have worked. But it didn't.
What else is different? In Level 1, the block moved along the NE diagonal — each click was NE of the previous position. In Level 2, the click (27,28) is NE of the square's bottom-right (37,18): Δ=(-10,+10). Exactly NE! So it should have worked...
Wait, maybe the movement is stepwise: the piece moves 1 cell per click?? In Level 1: click (53,10) from block center (59,4): the block moved 6 rows, 6 cols in one click. No, it was a big jump.
Hmm, wait. Let me re-verify: was the first click in Level 1 (53,10)? The output shows the first two lines as "click(53,10)" (duplicate, probably 2 transitions for 1 action, or the first transition was the seed). The block was initially at (58-60,3-5), center (59,4). After click (53,10): center (53,10). Δ=(-6,+6). A big jump along NE.
So why did Level 2's click (27,28) fail? Let me think... Maybe the piece can only move toward the ball, and (27,28) is... NE from the square, toward the ball. Hmm.
Or maybe there's a max step distance? Level 1's max was 6 (first click), then 2 each time. Level 2's click was 10 away. Maybe the max is 6?
Or maybe the click has to be within the ball's... no.
Or maybe the piece moves at most N cells per click, where N depends on something (W bar?). Level 1's W bar started at 62, and after 19 clicks was 56... shrinks by 2 per click.
Let me test: click (30,24) — 7 NE from the square's bottom-right (37,18): Δ=(-7,+6)? Not NE. For NE from (37,18): (37-t,18+t). t=7: (30,25). t=6: (31,24).
Let me try (31,24): 6 NE steps. If the square moves there, then the max distance is ≥6, and the rule is "click must be NE on the diagonal". Then continue.
Actually, wait — maybe the rule is: the click must be on the diagonal from the square's bottom-right, and the square moves to the click position. (27,28): from (37,18), Δ=(-10,+10) — on the diagonal. It should have worked. Unless the diagonal anchor is different: the square's center (36.5,17.5): (27,28): Δ=(-9.5,+10.5) — off by 1. If the anchor is the center and the click must be exactly on the NE diagonal from the center (i.e., click row - 36.5 == click col - 17.5 → click col - click row == 19): (27,28): 28-27=1 ≠ 19. Off by a lot. (31,24): 24-31=-7. No.
Hmm, the center anchor doesn't work for integer clicks (center is at .5). The bottom-right anchor (37,18): clicks on the NE diagonal satisfy col - row = 18-37 = -19: (27,28): 28-27=1 ≠ -19. Wait, I messed up: NE diagonal from (37,18): points (37-t, 18+t): col - row = (18+t)-(37-t) = 2t-19. For t=10: 1. So (27,28) is on the NE diagonal from (37,18) (t=10: 37-10=27, 18+10=28). Yes, on the diagonal.
So both the center (approximately) and the bottom-right are consistent... ugh.
Let me think about it differently. Maybe the piece only moves if the click is within a certain distance. Test with a smaller jump: click (33,22) (t=4: 37-4=33, 18+4=22). If it moves → distance is not the issue (or ≤4). Then continue with more clicks.
Actually, let me reconsider the trail: in Level 1, the trail pixels were at (57,6),(55,8),(51,12),(49,14),... — these are exactly the click positions minus... click (53,10): trail (55,8) is between (59,4) and (53,10): on the path. The trail was at every other cell of the path: (58,5)? not in the list; (57,6) is; (56,7)? no; (55,8) is; (54,9)? no. So the trail is at odd steps. The block animated through the intermediate cells.
OK, another thought: maybe the piece moves at a fixed speed (1 cell per tick), and each click sets the target; the piece moves toward the target. The frame we see is after the piece has fully arrived (or after some animation frames). In Level 2, the click (27,28) was rejected because... it's outside the board? No. Because the path is blocked? The path from the square to (27,28) is a straight NE diagonal: cells (36,19),(35,20),...,(28,27) — all empty. No obstacles.
Hmm, wait a sec. Maybe the click must not be inside the ball's bounding box, or the piece can't enter a certain zone? (27,28) is adjacent to the ball's left edge (col 29). The target square (26-27,27-28) doesn't overlap the ball. No issue.
Let me look at the dots again: (37,41),(40,37),(54,49),(55,14),(56,47),(57,16). And the square at (36-37,17-18) — its bottom-right (37,18) coincides with where the dot was. The dot pairs: left pair: (37,18) & (41,16); right pair: (37,41) & (40,37); far right: (54,49) & (56,47); far left: (55,14) & (57,16).
Notice: (41,16) and (57,16) are both in col 16; (40,37) and (56,47)... the partner dots form a line with the first dot: left pair: (37,18)→(41,16): Δ=(+4,-2). Far left: (55,14)→(57,16): Δ=(+2,+2). Right pair: (37,41)→(40,37): Δ=(+3,-4). Far right: (54,49)→(56,47): Δ=(+2,-2).
Hmm, no consistent pattern.
New idea: maybe the dots are "targets" where the square should be placed (like sockets), and the square moves from dot to dot? The square is currently on dot (37,18). The next dot in the sequence is... (41,16)? That's SW of the ball. Hmm, but the goal is the ball.
Or maybe the dots are just decorative "stars".
Let me try a discriminating probe: click (33,22) (4 NE from the square's bottom-right, on the diagonal). If the square moves there → the teleport works for short NE moves; then the failure at (27,28) was due to distance (max ~6?) or something else. If it doesn't move → the constraint is different (maybe the click must be on a dot, or in a specific direction).
